steps.title: Four stages, and no secure monitor
steps.body:
From power-on to a login prompt, each stage loads the next. Unlike the other boards of this repository there is no TF-A and no OP-TEE: the Zynq-7000 is a 32-bit SoC whose Cortex-A9 cores start in the secure state, and Linux simply runs there.

The interesting part is stage 2: U-Boot's own SPL does the job that Xilinx's FSBL does in vendor flows.

steps.title: The BootROM is the only code you cannot change
steps.body:
A 128 KiB mask ROM inside the chip. At power-on it latches the mode pins (jumper **JP5** on the Eclypse Z7), and in SD mode it reads the card's MBR, finds the first FAT partition and opens a file named `BOOT.BIN`.

If the jumper is wrong or the file is missing, nothing is printed at all.

steps.title: It validates a header before it trusts the file
steps.body:
`BOOT.BIN` starts with a 2,240-byte header: a width-detection word, the identifier `XNLX`, the payload offset and a checksum. The ROM checks them and copies the payload into the 256 KiB on-chip RAM (OCM) at address 0, then jumps there.

The next diagram, *Inside BOOT.BIN*, shows every field.

steps.title: The SPL is the first-stage loader, and it is U-Boot
steps.body:
The same U-Boot source tree builds a tiny first stage (the SPL, *secondary program loader*) that fits in the on-chip RAM. `mkimage -T zynqimage` wraps it in the header above and it becomes `BOOT.BIN`.

No Vivado or Vitis is needed on your PC for this.

steps.title: ps7_init makes the DRAM usable
steps.body:
The first thing the SPL does is run `ps7_init()`: about a thousand register writes that start the PLLs, program the DDR3L controller, set the clock dividers and mux the MIO pins. Without it there is no memory and no serial port.

These values are generated by Vivado for the board's hardware design, so the build downloads a pinned file (see chapter 03).

steps.title: U-Boot proper is a separate file, loaded by name
steps.body:
The SPL opens `u-boot.img` on the same FAT partition and loads it to `0x04000000` in DDR. This is the full bootloader with a shell, drivers and distro boot; it relocates itself to the top of RAM.

It looks for `/extlinux/extlinux.conf`, reads the kernel (`zImage` at `0x02000000`) and the device tree (`0x01F00000`) and runs `bootz`.

steps.title: Linux starts from the zImage and a device tree
steps.body:
The zImage unpacks itself, the device tree tells it where the UART, the SD controller and the Ethernet MAC are, and `root=PARTUUID=…-02` selects the ext4 partition. Then `/sbin/init` runs and a login appears on `ttyPS0`.

The second Cortex-A9 is started by the kernel through the SCU and SLCR registers: there is no PSCI firmware.

steps.title: Each hand-over is a file name
steps.body:
ROM to SPL: `BOOT.BIN` in the FAT root. SPL to U-Boot: `u-boot.img`. U-Boot to Linux: whatever `extlinux.conf` names. If a stage does not appear on the console, the file before it is the first suspect.

The troubleshooting chapter lists the first log line of each failure.

steps.anchor: Programmable logic (PL): never configured in this build. UART, SD card and Ethernet are PS peripherals on MIO pins, so they work without it.
steps.title: The FPGA half of the chip stays empty
steps.body:
The Zynq also contains an FPGA (the PL). Nothing here loads a bitstream, and nothing needs one: the console, the SD card and Ethernet are hard peripherals of the processing system on MIO pins.

A bitstream becomes necessary only for the Zmod ADC modules (chapter 13).
